summary: Umpqua NF summit in Douglas County, OR: a 22-foot L-4 tower built 1934-35 with a 1935 fire save, removed in 1965; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 14-by-14 L-4 cab on a 22-foot round timber tower
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1965 (register) or destroyed that year (firelookout.com); no source describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: Charles Neal was the lookout in August 1935

events.note: 14-by-14 L-4 cab constructed on a 22-foot round timber tower, per the Oregon lookouts page
22-foot wooden L-4 tower built, per the register and firelookout.com; they differ from the 1934 cab date
Charles Neal listed as lookout at Kelsay Mountain
Fire near the Lemalo Falls canyon on the North Umpqua River, started by unregistered campers; spotted and trenched by Neal and held to about a quarter acre
12-by-20-foot pole and shake garage constructed for $56
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.supports: built 1935 as a 22-foot L-4 tower; removed 1965
evidence.quote: Built in 1935, this 22' wooden L-4 tower was removed in 1965.

evidence.supports: 1934 14-by-14 L-4 cab on a 22-foot round timber tower
evidence.quote: 1934: A 14 x 14 hip roofed L-4 lookout cab constructed on a 22-foot round timber tower.

evidence.supports: Charles Neal as lookout credited with saving Lemalo Falls canyon; fire started by unregistered campers
evidence.quote: Charles Neal, lookout at Kelsay Mountain, is credited by Mr. Harpham with saving the Lemalo falls canyon of the North Umpqua river from a disastrous fire, which was started through carelessness on the part of unregistered campers.

evidence.supports: Umpqua supervisor V.V. Harpham commended Neal
evidence.quote: V.V. Harpham, Supervisor of the Umpqua national forest

evidence.supports: Neal spotted the smoke, sent an alarm
evidence.quote: Neal spotted the smoke from the fresh fire, sent in an alarm

evidence.supports: Neal ran most of the way to the fire
evidence.quote: He ran the major portion of the way

evidence.supports: Neal ran to the fire; trenched and held to about a quarter acre before CCC crews arrived
evidence.quote: had the fire trenched, under control and confined to an area of about a quarter of an acre by the time men from the Diamond Lake CCC camp arrived.

evidence.quote: Kelsay Mountain Lookout site 2007 - courtesy of Ron Kemnow

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Oregon lookouts page dates the 14-by-14 cab to 1934 on a 22-foot tower; the register and firelookout.com date the 22-foot tower to 1935. The story gives both years and does not pick one.
The register says the tower was removed in 1965; firelookout.com says destroyed that year. The story uses both words.

notes_for_editor: No source read describes what remains at the site or how to reach it, so the story says so. The 1934 vs 1935 date conflict is kept as is. The 1935 fire story rests on a News-Review article quoted by the Oregon lookouts page; the original clipping was not read.
